method: OPM data.opm.gov 'Federal Workforce Data' (FedScope successor) employment snapshot, 2026-05, downloaded via https://data.opm.gov/api/v1/files/employment/2026/05/1/download (parquet, 2,025,993 employee rows). Filtered to department_code EP (EPA), NN (NASA), GS (GSA), SE (SEC), FD (FDIC). The file includes an `occupational_category` column (OPM's PATCO-equivalent classification: PROFESSIONAL / ADMINISTRATIVE / TECHNICAL / CLERICAL / OTHER WHITE COLLAR / BLUE COLLAR / INVALID) plus `occupational_series` and `pay_plan`. For each agency: (1) computed the categorical composition and pay-plan composition (Federal Wage System = wage-grade trades) to establish a base eligible/excluded split; (2) drilled into the top occupational series within each category to identify specific field-operational, hands-on-technical, or trades sub-populations the categorical split alone doesn't separate out (e.g., a 'Professional'-coded scientist who is actually a field inspector), and applied documented, sourced, arithmetic-explicit exclusions for those; (3) corroborated with public sources (GAO reports, agency careers/workforce pages, NASA OIG audit, FDIC examiner program materials). All five agencies came back with negligible or zero Federal Wage System (blue-collar trades) headcount, consistent with each agency contracting out its facilities/trades/security work rather than employing it directly -- the structural reason these five land far closer to 1.0 than typical CFO Act agencies.

rows.headcount_source_title: EPA Staffing Fact Sheet — Environmental Protection Network (citing EPA internal staffing plan sent to OMB, obtained via FOIA)
rows.headcount_quote: As of September 2025, EPA had 12,198 staff... 25% (about 4,000 staff) below Pre-Trump levels (16,155).
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: OPM data.opm.gov Federal Workforce Data, 2026-05 snapshot (department_code=EP, n=12,557 employees -- a later, smaller snapshot than the 12,198 Sept-2025 headcount carried forward, consistent with continued attrition): occupational_category -- PROFESSIONAL 7,556 (60.2%), ADMINISTRATIVE 4,749 (37.8%), CLERICAL 167 (1.3%), OTHER WHITE COLLAR 51 (0.4%), TECHNICAL 26 (0.2%), BLUE COLLAR 1 (0.0%), INVALID 7 (0.1%). Only 1 of 12,557 employees is on a Federal Wage System (trades/wage-grade) pay plan -- EPA does not directly employ its own facilities/janitorial/trades staff (GSA-managed or contracted buildings). Excluded: BLUE COLLAR (1) + INVALID (7); series 1811 Criminal Investigation (205 employees, 1.6% of workforce) -- EPA's Criminal Investigation Division special agents, armed federal law enforcement conducting field investigations, not desk knowledge work; and an estimated 25% of series 0028 Environmental Protection Specialist (1,171 total employees; 293 excluded) representing facility compliance inspectors and Superfund on-scene coordinators whose primary duty is on-site work, versus the majority of the series who are HQ/regional policy, permit-review, and program-analysis staff. (EPA's own enforcement materials confirm inspection requires field presence but publish no inspector headcount; EPA notes most day-to-day facility inspections nationally are conducted by state agencies under delegated authority, so the field-primary share of 0028 is treated as a minority, not majority, of the series -- this 25% split is a judgment estimate, not independently sourced, hence confidence=medium.) Total excluded = 1 + 7 + 205 + 293 = 506 of 12,557 = 4.0%. Eligible share = 1 - 0.040 = 0.960.
rows.notes: EPA's own careers page (epa.gov/careers/what-kind-people-work-epa) lists occupations as 'accountants and budget specialists, attorneys, biologists, chemists, communications and public affairs specialists, computer/information technology specialists, economists, engineers, financial specialists, human resources specialists, management analysts, physical scientists, social scientists, and toxicologists' alongside a separate, smaller set of field/technical roles: 'lab technicians, law enforcement agents, and intelligence research specialists' -- corroborating the categorical split (overwhelming majority desk-based professional/admin, with a distinct but small carve-out for field/lab/enforcement roles). No published inspector or lab-technician headcount was found (epa.gov/enforcement/fact-sheet-epas-civil-enforcement-program describes the enforcement process but has no staffing numbers), which is why the 0028 field-inspection split is an estimate rather than a sourced figure. Carried-forward W3 context: EPA fell from a 16,155 baseline to 12,198 by Sept 2025 (-24%) via RIF + Fork-in-the-Road/DRP/VERA, with ORD eliminated and EJ/DEI offices RIF'd; separate reporting projected further decline toward ~9,700 by early 2026.

rows.headcount_source_title: One Fifth of NASA's Workforce Take Voluntary Departure Options (SpacePolicyOnline.com, July 26, 2025)
rows.headcount_quote: NASA's expected remaining civil servant workforce following both DRP programs, as well as normal attrition (about 500) over the same time period: about 14,000.
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: OPM data.opm.gov Federal Workforce Data, 2026-05 snapshot (department_code=NN, n=13,962): occupational_category -- PROFESSIONAL 9,958 (71.3%), ADMINISTRATIVE 3,432 (24.6%), OTHER WHITE COLLAR 246 (1.8%, includes 209 Engineering/Architecture Student Trainees, kept eligible as desk-based analytical interns), TECHNICAL 243 (1.7%: series 0802 Engineering Technical 184 + 0856 Electronics Technical 46 + smaller series), CLERICAL 83 (0.6%). Zero employees on a Federal Wage System pay plan (0 of 13,962) -- NASA's genuine hands-on trades capacity (machinists, welders, wind-tunnel technicians, described in nasa.gov's 'Small Steps, Giant Leaps' podcast episodes 115-116 on 'Trade and Technical Professionals') is delivered predominantly through support-service contractors at NASA centers, not through NASA's own civil-servant wage-grade workforce, which is essentially absent from this headcount. Excluded = TECHNICAL 243 only (no Blue Collar or Invalid present in this snapshot). 243 / 13,962 = 1.7%. Eligible share = 1 - 0.017 = 0.983, rounded to 0.98. This treats the bulk of the 0861 Aerospace Engineering (3,514, 25.2%) and 0801 General Engineering (2,869, 20.5%) series as desk/analysis-based (modern spaceflight engineering is simulation- and model-heavy) rather than hands-on fabrication, since no agency-specific data was found to split engineers' time between design work and physical test/integration work -- this is the main judgment call limiting confidence to medium rather than high.
rows.notes: NASA OIG's STEM workforce audit and other NASA workforce materials describe ~60-63% of NASA's civil-service workforce as science/engineering (S&E), with roughly 85% of that S&E cadre being engineers and ~10% scientists -- consistent with the parquet's PROFESSIONAL share (71.3%) once administrative/support staff are netted out. NASA's own recruiting materials (nasa.gov/learning-resources career-spotlight pages, welder/machinist postings) confirm a real but small in-house hands-on trades cadre; JPL (Caltech-operated FFRDC, ~4,500-6,000 staff) is not counted in this civil-servant headcount at all, consistent with W3's finding. Carried-forward W3 context: NASA fell from a 17,391 pre-RIF baseline to ~14,000 by July 2025 (-22%) via two DRP rounds + VERA/VSIP + attrition; FY2026 budget projects a further drop to 11,853 if involuntary RIFs proceed (unconfirmed forward projection).

rows.headcount_quote: The FY 2026 request includes a decrease in FTE from the FY 2025 Enacted, going from 5,455 to 4,195 [PBS]; 3,436 full-time equivalent (FTE) employees [FAS/ASF]; 692 [S&E]
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: OPM data.opm.gov Federal Workforce Data, 2026-05 snapshot (department_code=GS, n=8,323 -- an exact match to the W3 headcount, so this parquet snapshot is very likely the underlying source for that figure): occupational_category -- ADMINISTRATIVE 4,274 (51.4%), PROFESSIONAL 2,333 (28.0%), CLERICAL 1,480 (17.8%), TECHNICAL 190 (2.3%), OTHER WHITE COLLAR 29 (0.3%), BLUE COLLAR 17 (0.2%). Excluded: BLUE COLLAR (17, in-house trades); series 0809 Construction Control Technical (123) and 0802 Engineering Technical (59), 182 combined, on-site construction/renovation inspection roles with substantial field time; an estimated 30% of series 2150 Transportation Operations (255 total; 77 excluded) representing GSA Fleet motor-pool/dispatch staff with hands-on vehicle duties, versus the majority who administer the Fleet program. Total excluded = 17 + 123 + 59 + 77 = 276 of 8,323 = 3.3%. Eligible share = 1 - 0.033 = 0.967, rounded to 0.97. The 30% Transportation Operations split is a judgment estimate (no GSA-published breakdown of Fleet program admin vs. hands-on motor-pool staff was found), which is why confidence is medium rather than high.
rows.notes: GSA's own career materials describe 'Building Management Specialists' (series 1176, 662 employees, 8.0% of the workforce) as overseeing/operating the federal real-estate portfolio, not performing trades work themselves -- consistent with GSA's building trades, janitorial, and security work being contracted out under the Service Contract Act rather than performed by GSA direct-hires (per federal contracting-guide sources describing SCA wage coverage for GSA-building janitors/floor technicians). This is the structural reason 1176 is treated as eligible desk/oversight work rather than excluded, and why GSA's Federal Wage System headcount is only 0.2% of the agency. Carried-forward W3 context: GSA fell -33% vs. a 12,500 Wave-1 baseline; later reporting (GSA OIG via GovExec, Apr 2026) suggests PBS alone fell further to ~3,100 by end of 2025; TTS down 67% since Jan 2025 and 18F (~90 people) eliminated entirely.

rows.headcount_source_title: SEC FY 2026 Congressional Budget Justification, corroborated by SEC Chairman Atkins's May 2025 town hall
rows.headcount_quote: at its height last year, the SEC had a total of 5,000 employees and 2,000 contractors, and that today it is down to approximately 4,200 employees and 1,700 contractors
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: OPM data.opm.gov Federal Workforce Data, 2026-05 snapshot (department_code=SE, n=3,941 -- lower than the 4,200 May-2025 headcount carried forward, consistent with SEC's well-documented continued 2025-2026 downsizing): occupational_category -- PROFESSIONAL 2,578 (65.4%), ADMINISTRATIVE 1,320 (33.5%), CLERICAL 40 (1.0%), OTHER WHITE COLLAR 1, TECHNICAL 1, INVALID 1. Zero Blue Collar; zero Federal Wage System pay-plan employees. Top series are entirely desk/knowledge-work: 0905 General Attorney (1,685, 42.8%), 0510 Accounting (649, 16.5%), 1831 Securities Compliance Examining (375, 9.5%), 2210 IT Management (280, 7.1%). Excluded = INVALID (1) only; 1/3,941 = 0.03%. Raw eligible = 0.9997, rounded down to 0.99 (not 1.00) to reserve for a handful of building-security-liaison / mailroom-type positions too small to register as a distinct series in this snapshot -- SEC leases its office space and does not directly employ facilities-trades staff.
rows.notes: GAO's SEC personnel surveys (GAO-23-106234, and predecessor GAO-20-304sp) identify the SEC's five 'mission-critical occupations' as attorneys, accountants, examiners, economists, and IT specialists -- i.e., GAO itself frames the entire top of SEC's occupational structure as desk-based knowledge work, directly corroborating the parquet composition. Securities Compliance Examiners inspect broker-dealers/investment advisers on-site but primarily review filings/records, so are treated as eligible per the task's examiner-role convention (consistent with FDIC's treatment below). Carried-forward W3 context: SEC fell -8.7% vs. a 4,600 Wave-1 baseline; GAO-26-107813 reports ~18% of SEC staff departed FY2025 via buyout/deferred-resignation (no RIF); FY2026 request FTE ceiling is 4,101.

rows.headcount_source_title: FDIC staff reductions raise watchdog concerns (American Banker)
rows.headcount_quote: The total workforce, which was more than 6,300 employees at the end of 2024, fell to just over 5,000 by Jan. 1, 2026
rows.ai_eligible_rationale: OPM data.opm.gov Federal Workforce Data, 2026-05 snapshot (department_code=FD, n=5,046 -- closely matches the 5,000 headcount as of Jan 2026 carried forward): occupational_category -- ADMINISTRATIVE 4,089 (81.0%, dominated by series 0570 Financial Institution Examining, 2,369 employees, 46.9% of the agency), PROFESSIONAL 557 (11.0%), CLERICAL 368 (7.3%), OTHER WHITE COLLAR 32 (0.6%). Zero Blue Collar, zero Technical, zero Invalid, zero Federal Wage System pay-plan employees -- FDIC has no in-house trades/facilities workforce (its offices are leased/GSA-managed, not FDIC-operated). Per the task's framing, FDIC bank examiners travel (a reported 75% travel requirement per fdic.gov careers materials) but conduct examinations primarily via laptop against bank records: FDIC's own 'e-Exam' program (fdic.gov/bank-examinations/examiners-desk-e-exam) describes examiners retrieving bank data images remotely over encrypted sessions, and FDIC negotiated a home-based telework option specifically for examiners (fdic.gov/careers/fdic-telework-options; 80% of the agency elected home-based telework per FDIC/GovExec reporting) -- confirming the examiner's primary work tool is a laptop doing desk/knowledge work, not physical/manual labor. No occupational category is excluded in this snapshot; raw eligible = 1.00, rounded down to 0.99 to reserve for unclassified building-security/mailroom-type roles too small to register as a distinct series, and for FDIC's small in-house OIG investigative function which is a separate reporting entity not clearly isolable within this department-code slice.
rows.notes: The task's own framing anticipated this result ('bank examiners travel but work laptops') and the parquet + FDIC's own e-Exam and telework materials directly corroborate it -- examiners are the single largest occupational series at FDIC (46.9%) and are travel-based but laptop-centric, not field/manual. Carried-forward W3 context: FDIC fell -20.6% vs. a 6,300 end-2024 baseline; FDIC's 2026 Operating Budget board memo sets 2026 authorized staffing (ex-OIG) at 5,386, '1,337 fewer than initially approved as part of the 2025 budget,' following a 2025 Workforce Optimization Initiative.
